skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted (major): The 'could' to 'has' shift is real (BMY:10k_FY2025.md p27: 'The expanded utilization of the 340B program in recent years has negatively affected our revenues and profit margins'), but it is not BMS-specific news. Peers already wrote 340B as a realized drag in the same filing season: Merck (MRK:10k_FY2025.md p39: 'increased utilization of the 340B Federal Drug Discount Program ... are having a negative impact on the Company's performance') and Amgen (AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p38: 'has had, and is expected to continue to have, a negative impact'). AbbVie, Gilead and Pfizer still use hedged language (ABBV p23, GILD p21, PFE p19), so BMS is catching up to peers, not leading. Management also said it plainly on the 2025Q1 call (BMY:companies/BMY/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p11, grade C, Boerner: 'we continue to be very focused on and concerned about abuses in the 340B program'), and 340B is listed in the forward-looking risk list of every 2025-2026 earnings release (e.g. BMY:earnings/2026-07-30 release p10). Every shortlist pharma has 340B exposure to roughly the same degree, which is the brief's 'every company has it' kill. The charge-back growth (22% vs 5% gross sales) is an upper bound that also holds DoD/VA and cash discounts and, in 2025-26, price-protection on the January 2026 Eliquis WAC cut, so it cannot be pinned on 340B. Correction: Narrow to: BMS joined Merck and Amgen in describing 340B as a realized drag in FY2025. It becomes non-obvious only if the 340B share of the $14.1B charge-back line can be sized (not disclosed), or if BMS's charge-back growth can be shown to exceed peers' on a comparable basis.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: held (minor): Settled on the specific question. I re-read BMY:10k_FY2025.md p49 and the arithmetic checks: at the 2024 rate (11,510/83,671 = 13.76%), 2025 charge-backs would have been $12,117M against $14,067M actual, an excess of $1,950M. Medicaid/Medicare rebates at the 2024 rate would have been $17,424M against $18,010M, an excess of only $586M. Nowhere in the sources does management or an analyst say that the charge-back line led the widening. Searching all ten BMS transcripts (2024Q1-2026Q2), the five 2025-26 earnings releases and the policy press releases for 'charge-back', 'chargeback', 'DoD', 'VA', 'covered entit' and 'channel mix' gives zero hits in any call. Management's own framing points the other way. The Q4 2025 release blames 'higher U.S. government channel rebates' (BMY:earnings/2026-02-05 release p2 and p6), and the 10-K's driver sentence on p49 credits 'the redesign of the U.S. Medicare Part D program and higher government channel mix'. Both read as a rebate and Part D story, while the line that actually grew 22% is charge-backs (p83 says it holds 340B, DoD/VA and cash discounts, settled as credits against receivables). The only 340B remark on any call is Boerner's policy comment on 2025Q1 ('concerned about abuses in the 340B program', BMY:companies/BMY/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p11), which is not about BMS's own numbers. 340B is not even a tracked topic in market/never_asked.csv or priced_in_scorecard.csv for BMY. The composition is therefore not said, not asked, and runs against management's stated explanation. Correction: Hold only this claim: in 2025 the charge-back line (340B, DoD/VA, cash discounts), not Medicaid/Medicare rebates, made up about $1.95B (~78%) of BMS's ~$2.5B gross-to-net excess, while management described the widening as Part D and government-channel rebates, and no analyst has asked about it. The 'could' to 'has' wording drift stays dead as a standalone point because peers use the same language. The 340B share of the line remains unsized, so the claim must say 'charge-backs', not '340B'. Conceded: The materiality skeptic is right that the charge-back-led composition is a distinct and checkable point, and my round-1 kill only addressed the 340B wording, which is industry-wide. I checked the composition against every call and release in the index and found it was never stated or asked; management's explanation (Part D, 'government channel rebates') points to the wrong line. So I reverse c01 from refuted to held. Held: The 340B 'could' to 'has' wording drift on its own is still obvious: Merck 10-K p39 and Amgen 10-K p38 already use realized-tense language. I would not let the nugget lead with it. Narrowed: From '340B drift plus charge-backs' to the composition finding only: charge-backs, not Medicaid/Medicare rebates, drove ~78% of the 2025 U.S. gross-to-net excess, which contradicts management's 'rebates' framing. 340B is named only as one unsized component.

verdict_reason: Surviving claim: In FY2025 the charge-backs and cash discounts line (which the 10-K says holds DoD/VA and 340B program pricing plus ~2% prompt-pay discounts) accounted for about $1.95B, roughly 78%, of the ~$2.49B by which BMS's total company gross-to-net adjustments exceeded the 2024 rate, while Medicaid and Medicare rebates accounted for only ~$0.59B; but the mix is a Q4 2025 effect (through nine months the split was about even, $1.03B vs $1.11B), the 340B share is undisclosed, and the 10-K's own 'higher government channel mix' wording covers this line, so it is a composition fact, not a contradiction of management or a sized 340B drag. Both skeptics accept the p49 arithmetic (BMY:10k_FY2025.md p49: charge-backs 14,067 vs 11,510, +22%; gross 88,085 vs 83,671, +5%; Medicaid/Medicare 18,010 vs 16,551). Materiality refuted in round 2 because the line also holds DoD/VA, cash discounts and possibly price protection, so no 340B dollar is isolable; obviousness held it as never said and as contradicting the 'rebates and Part D' framing. I opened the sources. (1) Composition: confirmed arithmetic. At 2024 line rates on 2025 gross, excess is charge-backs $1,950M, Medicaid/Medicare $586M, other -$45M, total $2,490M (p49). This is total-company, not U.S.-only. (2) Timing: the 10-Q filed before the December 2025 government agreement and the January 2026 Eliquis list cut (BMY:companies/BMY/10q_2025Q3.md p36) shows nine-month 2025 charge-backs 9,840 vs 8,366 and Medicaid/Medicare 13,244 vs 11,525 on gross 64,548 vs 61,298: excess $1,030M charge-backs vs $1,108M rebates, an even split. The 78% comes from Q4 2025 (FY minus 9M): charge-backs 4,227 vs 3,144 (+34%) on gross +5%, Medicaid/Medicare 4,766 vs 5,026 (-5%). That quarter coincides with the U.S. Government Agreement announced December 2025 (BMY:10k_FY2025.md p44) and with the charge-back reserve nearly doubling to $1,720M from $900M (p48, p107). Note 2 lists 'pricing protection below wholesaler list price' among U.S. GTN types (p83), so the materiality skeptic's price-protection caveat is plausible though the line placement is not disclosed. The full-year rebate line is also depressed by a $342M Medicaid/Medicare prior-period release (p48); on current-period provisions the charge-back share is roughly 70% (estimate: the 2024 line split of prior-period changes is not on these pages). (3) Framing: the 10-K driver sentence is 'redesign of the U.S. Medicare Part D program and higher government channel mix' (p49), and p65 defines charge-backs as government-entity programs (DoD, VA) and 340B covered entities, so a charge-back-led widening is consistent with 'government channel mix'; the Q3 10-Q framing ('higher government channel rebates and mix, including ... Part D', p36) matches the even nine-month split. The contradiction is not supported; only the Q4 release's 'higher U.S. government channel rebates' wording (BMY:earnings/2026-02-05_a2025q4ex991.md p2, p6) is loose. (4) Persistence: H1 2026 charge-backs fell to 13.8% of gross from 15.1% (BMY:10q_2026Q2.md p31), so the 2025 excess did not carry forward as a rate. The 340B 'could' to 'has' drift is dead on obviousness (MRK and AMGN use the same tense). Composition is confirmed; its significance is unrefuted at best and probably a year-end timing/reserve effect.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted (major): Quotes and speaker verified: BMY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p1 is grade B, and the speakers are Adam Lenkowsky and Luisa Hector. In context, though, Lenkowsky's 'roughly equal' answers a question about Part D sales phasing. He says Eliquis sales are 'more even' through the year, offset by catastrophic-phase effects on Revlimid, Pomalyst and Camzyos. The filings (10-Q 2025Q3 p36; 10-K FY2025 p49) talk about the U.S. GTN rate. Those are different metrics, so this is not a like-for-like contradiction. The sizing also fails. The ~$2.9B (4 points x $71.7B U.S. gross) is a gross-deduction number, not a net revenue headwind, because the redesign also raises volume. The candidate text says $2.7B while the math says $2.9B, and the 49% and 53% are rounded (my back-solve from p83 and p49 gives ~3.8 points, about $2.7B). Worst of all, the 10-K line items do not let Part D be the 'primary' part of $2.9B. On p49, Medicaid and Medicare rebates (where Part D manufacturer discounts would land) were only ~$0.59B above the 2024 rate on 2025 gross; charge-backs were $1.95B. The 10-K driver sentence also names 'higher government channel mix' jointly with Part D. So the $1.15 EPS 'attributed mostly to Part D' is not supported, and it double-counts c01. Correction: Narrow to: the filings name Part D redesign plus government channel mix for a ~4-point U.S. GTN rise (~$2.7-2.9B of extra U.S. deductions, all of which were offset by $4.4B of gross growth). The Medicare/Medicaid rebate line contributed only ~$0.6B of the excess, so any Part D-specific sizing is at most about $0.6B unless BMS books Part D discounts elsewhere. The call remark was about sales phasing, not the GTN rate.

My line-item point stands: on BMY:10k_FY2025.md p49, Medicaid and Medicare rebates were only ~$0.59B above the 2024 rate. Correction: Narrow to: the 10-K names Part D and government channel mix for a ~4-point U.S. GTN rise. Any Part D-specific number is at most ~$0.6B (the Medicaid/Medicare line excess). Conceded: Their evidence that Part D was discussed on the 2024Q4 and 2025Q1 calls (grade C), and that the guidance request was taken up on later calls, removes the 'left unanswered' half. skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted (major): Part D redesign is one of the most-asked BMS topics. Louisa Hector asked BMS to quantify it on the 2024Q4 call (BMY:companies/BMY/transcripts/2024Q4_transcript.md p8-9, grade C). Lenkowsky answered 'there are pushes and pulls', and Elkins flagged 'additional gross to net pressures from Medicare Part D redesign' in prepared remarks (same doc, p6). On the 2025Q1 call Elkins blamed Eliquis's -3% quarter on Part D redesign and said immunology rebates rose because of it (BMY:companies/BMY/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p4). The priced_in_scorecard has IRA_negotiation as 'routinely asked' (19 analyst turns, 7 of 10 quarters) and gross_to_net_price asked in 5 of 10 quarters (market/priced_in_scorecard.csv#29, #32). I re-read the 2025Q3 grade-B quote (Lenkowsky, BMY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p1). His 'roughly equal' is about revenue: Eliquis gains from the removed coverage gap are offset by catastrophic-phase liability on Revlimid, Pomalyst and Camzyos. The 10-Q statement is about the U.S. GTN percentage. A higher GTN rate with flat net revenue impact is consistent, so the 'contradiction' mixes a dollar effect with a rate. The second half of the candidate, that the request to tighten 2026-27 Eliquis guidance went unanswered, was answered on the next call. On 2025Q4 (BMY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p1) Lenkowsky and Elkins explained the decision not to guide 2027, the 2026Q1 call gave a $1.5-2B 2027 step-down, and 2026Q2 reiterated it (BMY:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p1, Lenkowsky to Scala). All of these are grade C. Correction: If anything survives, it is narrower: the FY2025 10-K names Part D and government channel mix as the main driver of a 49% to 53% U.S. GTN rate. That shows the redesign shifted cost into rebates even though management called the revenue effect a wash. This is an explanation of a disclosed number, not something management hid.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted (major): The materiality skeptic's p49 split (Medicaid/Medicare rebates only ~$0.59B above the 2024 rate) strengthens my kill. If Part D discounts sit in that line, Part D cannot be the main driver of the extra deductions, so the call-vs-filing 'contradiction' falls apart on the numbers as well as on obviousness (Part D was asked on 2024Q4 p8-9 and answered on 2025Q1 p4). Their reading of Lenkowsky's remark as about sales phasing matches my reading of the 2025Q3 p1 transcript. Correction: Nothing in c02 survives on its own. Its only usable content, that the 10-K blames Part D and channel mix, belongs in narrowed c01 as the management framing that the charge-back composition contradicts. Conceded: Their p49 decomposition and their reading of the remark as about phasing are correct; I adopt both. Held: Refuted: Part D was asked and answered, and the remark was not about the GTN rate. Narrowed: Fold the 10-K driver sentence into c01 as the management claim that the numbers contradict.

verdict_reason: Both skeptics independently read Lenkowsky's grade-B remark (BMY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p1) as a revenue-phasing statement (Eliquis evened out, catastrophic-phase cost on Revlimid, Pomalyst, Camzyos), not a GTN-rate claim; the obviousness skeptic shows Part D was asked and answered on 2024Q4 and 2025Q1 (grade C) and the 2026-27 Eliquis guidance request was taken up on later calls. No disagreement remains. Confirmed refuted.
